newsitem.title: UK: UK service sector shows strong growth in May - PMI.
newsitem.headline: UK service sector shows strong growth in May - PMI.

text.p: Business conditions in the British services sector showed a further significant improvement in May, with the PMI business activity index rising to a new seasonally adjusted high of 64.8 from 61.2 in April, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
This was the 11th consecutive monthly increase, with just under 40 percent of companies reporting an increase in activity.
The survey, sponsored by Reuters, is based on information from 500 executives in private sector service industries, excluding retail and wholesale.
The rise in activity in May reflected an increase in the number of firms boosting capacity to meet strengthening demand for their services.
"The rate of growth of incoming new business has picked up significantly over the past seven months and accelerated again in May to record the largest monthly rise reported to date," the CIPS said.
Respondents generally expect business conditions to continue improving over the next year, driven largely by continued growth in the economy and especially by greater consumer spending on services.
Employment rose strongly again for the 11th month in a row, reflecting companies' need to expand capacity to meet current and anticipated future growth in demand for services.

"Despite the recruitment of new staff, another sharp increase in the overall amount of work outstanding at panel member companies suggests that the growth in demand continued to run ahead of the expansion of capacity," the CIPS said.
"Outstanding business has risen strongly so far this year in line with the faster growth of new business."
The rise in business outstanding was again partially explained by lack of suitably skilled personnel.
Skill shortages were reported in many sectors, especially in computing positions.
"The higher wages and salaries necessary to retain existing staff and to attract suitably qualified new personnel led to a further marked increase in costs during May."
Increasing numbers of service companies were reported to have raised their charges to maintain profit margins.
"On the whole, prices charged rose for the seventh consecutive month, with a modest acceleration in the rate of increase," the CIPS said.
However, strong competition continued to limit firms' ability to raise prices.
"Although a fifth of all companies reported a rise in costs, only 12 percent of companies were able to raise their charges."
Following are the main seasonally adjusted indices from the services survey:
May April
Business activity 64.8 61.2
Incoming new business 62.8 62.1
Outstanding business 57.9 53.5
Employment 56.6 55.4
Average prices charged 52.6 52.2
Average input prices 59.7 59.5
Business expectations 83.0 83.0
-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
